strengths.I003: A scoring-only change (bootstrap BT posterior plus cluster-correlated shift, greedy expected-max) that targets the selection stage directly, and can be tested fully offline by replaying saved pairwise records against best-of-3, with an on/off flag and a single labelling call per brief.
strengths.I006: It changes the ideas themselves at the development stage. Executed checks give concrete feedback, and a cross-run template library gives it something a lone agent cannot have. Its effect is measured as an outcome (falsified-claim rate under a held-out checker) rather than as rater opinion.

verdicts.reason: I003 needs 2-3 days, about 60 lines and almost no extra tokens, and its test is an offline replay. I006 needs one to two weeks, roughly doubles development tokens, has 7 open major critiques, and depends on an unverified assumption that executable check ledgers exist at development time.

strengths.I006: It improves idea substance through execution-grounded repair and reusable checks, and the gain is measured by an outcome (falsified-claim rate) that does not depend on judge taste. Verified claims help on any brief with checkable content.
strengths.I007: A cheap residual selector that falls back to internal BT when labels are scarce and zeroes the nuisance covariates (length, hedges, family match) at selection time. It is evaluated by leave-one-brief-out AUC on existing runs, and it explicitly learns the internal ranking's systematic error, which a lone agent never observes.

verdicts.reason: I007 is trained on benchmark verdicts, so from about 15 noisy briefs it mostly learns what the benchmark panel prefers, which puts it at risk of helping only on the benchmark. I006 makes the delivered ideas more correct on any brief whose claims can be checked.
